name: Botlikh

catalog_citation: Magomedbekova, Z. M. 1999. Botlikhskij jazyk. In: Jazyki mira: Kavkazskie jazyki, 228-236. Moskva: Academia. (HTML transcription at philology.ru/linguistics4/magomedbekova-99.htm). Secondary: Borise, Lena. 2018 ms. Word stress in the languages of the Caucasus…
catalog_locator: Magomedbekova 1999, section 2.1.2 (pp. 228-236 of the volume; HTML has no page breaks); Borise 2018 sec. 7.1 p. 18
catalog_quote: 2.1.2. Ударение слабое, динамическое, подвижное. Место ударения часто обусловлено морфологической структурой слова; при суф. - де ударение на финальном слоге ( ъамбур-дé ‘крыши’), при суф. - балъи - на предшествующем слоге ( ъимá-балъи ‘отцы’). Во множественном числе в косвенных падежах имен существительных ударение не меняется: им. п. геде ‘кошки’, эрг.п. гедé-ди . В единственном числе при склонении ударение часто перемещается. Ударение обладает дистинктивной функцией: гьúкьу ‘сказал’, гьикý ‘сказав’; или же бéкьи ‘хлев’ - бекьú ‘пахота’, масá! ‘скажи!’ - мáса ‘сказал’.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Russian passage is verbatim in the held at sec. 2.1.2 (lines 133-140), and the Borise 2018 sec. 7.1 secondary passage is verbatim in the held Borise txt. (2) Deciding source is a 1999 9-page encyclopedic grammar sketch (Jazyki mira) by a specialist; Glottolog lists only Gudava 1962 (264 pp, Georgian) and Gudava 1967 (14 pp) as descriptive works, and web search (HSE LingConLab, Verhees site, TALD, journals) finds no instrumental or dedicated phonological study of Botlikh stress — TALD has no stress chapter; the De Gruyter handbook chapter is still a 2022 draft. (3) downloaded that draft (Alexeyev & Verhees 2022, sec. 2.4 Prosody, p.5): it independently confirms 'weak, dynamic, movable' stress, stressed plural -dé/-é, pre-stressing -baɬi and =ma, singular oblique stress shift (ráša ~ rašú-ɬi, íma ~ imú-di) and distinctive minimal pai

sources.quote: 'Gudava and Magomedbekova treat stress in Botlikh as "weak, dynamic and movable" (Gudava 1967: 294; Magomedbekova 2001 (1999): 229). Its distinctive function shows in minimal pairs like béƛ̣'i 'cattle-shed' vs. beƛ̣'-í [plough-INF] or mas-á [tell-IMP] and más-a [tell-AOR]. Some patterns are governed by morphological conditions: the plural suffixes -dé and -é are always stressed. In plural forms with the suffix -baɬi, stress falls on the preceding vowel: íma 'father' imá-baɬi 'fathers'. The same effect occurs when the interrogative particle ma is attached to a word. Many nouns carry stress on t
sources.note: Newest description (fieldwork 2017-2019) with an explicit Prosody section; confirms morphologically conditioned + distinctive mobile stress and adds the absolutive-initial / oblique-second-syllable noun pattern; should be added as a co-source to lift the record off a single 1999 encyclopedic sketch.

tone.summary: Grammar sketch only (phonetics = vowel/consonant inventory, syllable, assimilation; then morphology, syntax, lexicon). Nothing on tone or pitch; stress only as acute marks on cited forms, uncommented.
